name: Vietnamese coffee
summary: Vietnamese coffee is usually robusta, brewed in a small metal phin filter. Ca phe sua da is iced coffee with condensed milk. Egg coffee, ca phe trung, is a Hanoi whipped-egg cup.
origin: Coffee growing is centered in the central highlands. The drinking culture is nationwide. Egg coffee is a Hanoi cafe invention. In Da Nang, the chairs on Bạch Đằng are the sitting-down cup, with the river in front of you.
howToEat: Wait for the phin to finish dripping. Stir the condensed milk up from the bottom.
Order nong (hot) or da (iced). Sua means milk.

In Hanoi, egg coffee is strong robusta under a sweet egg foam. Fold the foam in with a spoon. Have it in the afternoon in the Nguyễn Hữu Huân alley. Café Giảng, alley 39, is the door the tourism pages name for that cup.
where: In Da Lat, Vietnam National Authority of Tourism puts the hills around Cau Dat in Arabica country and names farm tours, including K'Ho. Drink it hot or iced after the lake walk. A stall price is not printed.
In Hanoi, the egg cup is the afternoon drink in the Nguyen Huu Huan alley.

In Ho Chi Minh City, the city itinerary names cà phê sữa đá at the cafes in the park outside the Reunification Palace, on a Saturday morning, before you go in. Visit HCMC names sidewalk coffee at Turtle Lake, traditional cloth-filter coffee, Do Phu Café, and the cafes in the 42 Nguyễn Huệ apartment building. No recipe was printed. The photograph is a glass on a wet table. It is not Turtle Lake.
priceBand: A sidewalk iced coffee is cheap. A designed cafe cup costs more and buys the chair.
